summary: R6 closure verified at dfae0b8: R6-NEW-MAJ-001 (correctness) — §6 024C/D/E/F Deliverable columns now conditional on cascade-status — CLOSED. findings.title: \S non-whitespace anchor absent from three downstream paraphrase descriptions of the meaningful-content spec: §5.2 line 135, §7 R-024-06 line 224, §7 R-024-07 line 225
findings.evidence:
Fix-round-6 introduced `\S.{19,}` (non-whitespace anchor) into invariant 2's canonical format spec and §6 024B's acceptance criterion. Three secondary description loci that paraphrase the meaningful-content requirement were not updated:

**Locus 1 — §5.2 line 135** (`blocked-on-adopter-conflict` definition):
'a `TF-024X-conflict-<adopter>` TF is filed + referenced in DISPATCH-NOTE **with meaningful content per invariant 2's regex spec** (status field + ≥20 char description; bare-prefix stub fails CI)'
Parenthetical says 'status field + ≥20 char description'. Omits the `\S` anchor. The canonical spec requires `\S.{19,}` — the description must START with a non-whitespace character. A description of '`(open):                    `' (20 spaces) satisfies '≥20 char description' but fails `\S`. An implementor consulting §5.2 to craft the `blocked-on-adopter-conflict` TF reference would not know the all-whitespace bypass is closed.

**Locus 2 — §7 R-024-06 line 224** (conflict-workflow CI enforcement):
'`check-invocation-log-entry.sh` (a) verifies the `TF-024X-conflict-<adopter>` reference IS present in DISPATCH-NOTE **with meaningful content matching invariant 2's regex spec** (status field + ≥20 char description; bare-prefix stubs fail CI)'
Same parenthetical gap: 'status field + ≥20 char description' omits `\S`. R-024-06 is the risk-surface row an implementor would consult to understand the conflict-close CI enforcement. The parenthetical summary is the operative guidance at this locus; 'matching invariant 2's regex spec' cross-references the spec but the parenthetical appears to fully enumerate what that spec requires — it does not.

**Locus 3 — §7 R-024-07 line 225** (Renovate-miss TF row guidance):
'the cascade slice MUST file a forward TF (`TF-024X-renovate-<adopter-slug>`) **as a STATUS.md "Tracked-forward items" row using exactly the standardised prefix `TF-024X-renovate-` followed by the adopter's `<owner>-<repo>` slug, with meaningful content** (status field + non-empty description after the slug — bare-prefix stubs fail the CI check per invariant 2)'
Parenthetical says 'status field + non-empty description after the slug'. This is the weakest paraphrase: it omits both the ≥20-char minimum AND the `\S` anchor. The 'per invariant 2' note appears only as a parenthetical aside to 'bare-prefix stubs fail'; it is not framed as 'for the full spec see invariant 2'. An implementor reading R-024-07 to know how to write the `TF-024X-renovate-<adopter-slug>` row in STATUS.md would conclude that any non-empty description suffices. A description like 'ok' (2 chars) passes 'non-empty' but fails `\S.{19,}` (minimum 20 chars). A description of 19 spaces passes 'non-empty' but fails both `\S` and `.{19,}` (needs 19 MORE chars after `\S`). A description of 20 spaces passes 'non-empty' and length but fails `\S`.

**Why MAJ:** This is the same defect class as R6-NEW-MAJ-001 (safety + completeness — regex prose mismatch between `.{20,}` and the 'non-whitespace' prose). That finding was MAJ on the grounds that a paraphrase of the spec that doesn't match the spec creates an exploitable gap: an implementor or CI-script author relying on the paraphrase writes the wrong check. Fix-round-6 fixed the canonical spec block (invariant 2) and the script acceptance criterion (§6 024B) but did not propagate to the three downstream paraphrase loci. These three loci are the descriptions an implementor would naturally consult when opening a `blocked-on-adopter-conflict` or `onboarded-operator-bump` cascade slice — §5.2 for the field requirements and §7 for the risk-row CI enforcement details. All three carry the pre-R6 'non-whitespace not mentioned' paraphrase.
findings.recommendation:
Update all three loci to include the `\S` non-whitespace qualifier:

**§5.2 line 135:** Replace '(status field + ≥20 char description; bare-prefix stub fails CI)' with '(format spec per invariant 2: `\S.{19,}` — description must start with a non-whitespace character + be ≥20 chars total; all-whitespace descriptions and bare-prefix stubs fail CI)'.

**§7 R-024-06 line 224:** Replace '(status field + ≥20 char description; bare-prefix stubs fail CI)' with the same correction: '(format spec per invariant 2: `\S.{19,}` — non-whitespace start + ≥20 chars total; all-whitespace descriptions and bare-prefix stubs fail CI)'.

**§7 R-024-07 line 225:** Replace '(status field + non-empty description after the slug — bare-prefix stubs fail the CI check per invariant 2)' with '(format spec per invariant 2: `\S.{19,}` — non-whitespace start + ≥20 chars total; single-char, short, and all-whitespace descriptions fail CI alongside bare-prefix stubs)'.

findings.title: DISPATCH-NOTE 'three-path' label stale at two loci after R6 added fail-closed as a fourth CI behaviour: risk item 4 and criterion (iii)
findings.evidence:
Fix-round-6 added the fail-closed default as a fourth CI behaviour (invariant 2, line 44). Two DISPATCH-NOTE sentences still describe the CI model as 'three-path':

**Locus A — DISPATCH-NOTE risk item 4 (line 69):**
'D-035's CI-refusal + invariant 2's **three-path CI enforcement** (per `cascade-status:` field — `onboarded` and `onboarded-operator-bump` paths require log entry + target match; `blocked-on-adopter-conflict` path requires log file NOT modified + TF reference with meaningful content per regex spec)'
The security mitigation is described as 'three-path CI enforcement'. The fail-closed default — which prevents silent bypass via an absent or mistyped `cascade-status:` field — is not named as part of the mitigation. The sentence cross-references 'invariant 2' by name in the row's plan-doc reference ('Plan-doc surfaces this as T-024-01 + T-024-02'), but the mitigation description itself does not cross-reference invariant 2's fail-closed explicitly.

**Locus B — DISPATCH-NOTE criterion (iii) (line 51):**
'operator-run + invocation-logged + CI-enforced (**three-path cascade-status**: `onboarded` / `onboarded-operator-bump` / `blocked-on-adopter-conflict`; positive evidence + meaningful-content regex match + negative assertion where applicable per invariant 2)'
The acceptance-criterion description of invariant 2 says 'three-path cascade-status' and enumerates the three declared values. The fail-closed default (absent/unrecognised → exit non-zero) is not named. 'per invariant 2' is present, making the fail-closed reachable in one hop, but a reviewer applying criterion (iii) as a standalone checklist item would not be prompted to verify the fail-closed specifically.

**Severity assessment (MIN, not MAJ):** Both loci cross-reference invariant 2 by name (Locus A: 'invariant 2's three-path CI enforcement'; Locus B: 'per invariant 2'). An implementor or auditor following those cross-references reaches invariant 2 where the fail-closed is explicit. The fail-closed cannot be omitted solely by reading these loci. Additionally, §5.2 line 132's 'MUST declare' + invariant 2 cross-reference correctly makes the fail-closed normatively effective. The DISPATCH-NOTE loci are descriptive (risk-surface and acceptance-criterion descriptions), not normative specs. The plan-doc invariant 2 IS correct and complete. This is a documentation-accuracy gap, not a specification defect that enables bypass.
findings.recommendation:
DISPATCH-NOTE risk item 4 (line 69): Replace 'invariant 2's three-path CI enforcement (per `cascade-status:` field — `onboarded` and `onboarded-operator-bump` paths require log entry + target match; `blocked-on-adopter-conflict` path requires log file NOT modified + TF reference with meaningful content per regex spec)' with 'invariant 2's four-behaviour CI enforcement (per `cascade-status:` field — `onboarded` and `onboarded-operator-bump` paths require log entry + target match; `blocked-on-adopter-conflict` path requires log file NOT modified + TF reference with meaningful content per regex spec; absent or unrecognised `cascade-status:` value exits non-zero, preventing template-drift bypass)'.

DISPATCH-NOTE criterion (iii) (line 51): Replace 'three-path cascade-status: `onboarded` / `onboarded-operator-bump` / `blocked-on-adopter-conflict`; positive evidence + meaningful-content regex match + negative assertion where applicable per invariant 2' with 'four-behaviour cascade-status CI enforcement per invariant 2: three named paths (`onboarded` / `onboarded-operator-bump` / `blocked-on-adopter-conflict`) with positive evidence + meaningful-content `\S.{19,}` regex match + negative assertion where applicable, plus fail-closed default (absent/unrecognised `cascade-status:` → CI exits non-zero)'.

fixpoint_status.fixpoint_criterion: 0 new CRIT + 0 new MAJ on a complete cycle
fixpoint_status.pattern_observation:
Seven consecutive rounds have caught propagation gaps in the cascade-status / invocation-log / meaningful-content spec clause. The concept-level sweep at R7 reveals one remaining MAJ defect class: fix-round-6 updated the canonical spec (invariant 2 format-spec block) and the script-implementation acceptance criterion (§6 024B) for the `\S` non-whitespace anchor but did not propagate to the three downstream paraphrase loci (§5.2 line 135, §7 R-024-06 line 224, §7 R-024-07 line 225) that describe the meaningful-content requirement in prose form. These paraphrase loci are where an implementor opening a `blocked-on-adopter-conflict` or `onboarded-operator-bump` cascade slice would naturally read for the TF-reference requirement — they are the operative descriptions for those paths.

For fix-round-8 (or whatever round follows): the fix is mechanical — replace the three parenthetical paraphrases with the explicit `\S.{19,}` format-spec reference (matching the canonical invariant 2 prose), then verify the DISPATCH-NOTE 'three-path' labels are updated to 'four-behaviour' per R7-NEW-MIN-001. After those four edits (three in plan-doc §5.2/§7, one in DISPATCH-NOTE for each of risk item 4 and criterion iii), the plan-doc + DISPATCH-NOTE should have no remaining loci where the meaningful-content spec is paraphrased without `\S` and no remaining loci where the CI model is described as 'three-path' without referencing the fail-closed. That would constitute the fixpoint condition.
